editorialSummary.heading: What families should know about the revised Austin ISD calendar
highlights: A Tuesday, August 18 start and Thursday, May 27 finish
Winter time off continues through the January 4 staff-development day
October 9 and March 26 can become attendance days after bad weather
paragraphs: Austin ISD revised the 2026-27 calendar in May 2026, increasing instructional days from 169 to 171. Students begin Tuesday, Aug. 18, and finish Thursday, May 27. Sept. 21 is a student holiday and PLED day, while Oct. 9 is listed as a student/staff holiday and possible bad-weather make-up day.

Fall break runs Nov. 23-27. Students are off Dec. 21-Jan. 4 and return Tuesday, Jan. 5; Jan. 4 is separately marked as a staff-development/student-holiday date. Parent-conference student holidays fall on Oct. 12 and Mar. 10, and spring break runs Mar. 15-19.

Mar. 26 is the calendar’s second possible bad-weather make-up day, and Apr. 30 is the second PLED/student holiday. The calendar also lists observances such as Yom Kippur, Diwali and Eid al-Fitr; an observance label does not by itself mean schools are closed.

faqs.question: When does Austin ISD start school in 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The first day of classes is Tuesday, August 18, 2026. New-teacher orientation, staff development, and teacher planning earlier in August are not student attendance days.

faqs.question: What is the last day of school for Austin ISD?
faqs.answer: Students finish Thursday, May 27, 2027. May 28 is a teacher planning day after classes end, so it is not included as a student event.

faqs.question: When is Austin ISD fall break?
faqs.answer: Fall break runs Monday, November 23, through Friday, November 27, 2026. Students leave after classes November 20 and return Monday, November 30.

faqs.question: When is Austin ISD winter break, and when do students return?
faqs.answer: Students are off from December 21 through January 4 and return Tuesday, January 5. Austin ISD’s English Important Dates list includes January 4 in the Winter Break range, while the calendar grid and Spanish Important Dates list label January 4 separately as Staff Development / Student Holiday.

faqs.question: When is Austin ISD spring break in 2027?
faqs.answer: Spring break is Monday, March 15, through Friday, March 19, 2027. Classes resume Monday, March 22 unless the district announces a separate schedule change.

faqs.question: Are October 9 and March 26 guaranteed student holidays?
faqs.answer: No. Both dates are labeled as student/staff holidays and bad-weather make-up days. If Austin ISD needs replacement instructional time, either date may become a required school day.

faqs.question: Why are students off on September 21?
faqs.answer: September 21 is a student holiday and PLED day, and the calendar also notes Yom Kippur. Students on the traditional calendar do not attend classes.

faqs.question: Are there classes during the October 12 parent conferences?
faqs.answer: No. October 12 is a student holiday with elementary and secondary parent conferences and an Indigenous Peoples’ Day observance. Families should get their individual conference time from the campus.

faqs.question: Do students attend school on November 2 and November 3?
faqs.answer: No. November 2 is a student/staff holiday, and November 3 is a student holiday with campus staff development. Students return Wednesday, November 4.

faqs.question: Is February 15 a school day on the traditional calendar?
faqs.answer: No. February 15 is a student holiday and campus staff-development day on Austin ISD’s Traditional Calendar. ADSY campuses follow a different schedule and dismiss students early that day.

faqs.question: Is there school in Austin ISD on March 10, 2027?
faqs.answer: March 10 is a student holiday for elementary and secondary parent conferences, with Eid al-Fitr also noted on the calendar. Students do not attend regular classes.

faqs.question: Why are students out on April 30?
faqs.answer: April 30 is a student holiday and Austin ISD’s second PLED day of the school year. Classes are scheduled to resume Monday, May 3.

faqs.question: When do Austin ISD grading periods end?
faqs.answer: The four grading periods end October 8 and December 18, 2026, then March 12 and May 27, 2027. The fourth period ends on the final student day.

faqs.question: What changed in Austin ISD’s revised 2026-27 calendar?
faqs.answer: Austin ISD increased the calendar from 169 to 171 instructional days. The district says the May 2026 revision added one school day in October and another in February.

faqs.question: How many instructional days are in the Austin ISD 2026-27 calendar?
faqs.answer: The revised traditional calendar has 171 instructional days. Austin ISD announced the increase from 169 days after the Board adopted the changes in May 2026.

faqs.question: What does PLED mean in Austin ISD?
faqs.answer: PLED means Professional Learning Exchange Day. Eligible campus-based exempt staff can exchange 12 hours of qualifying professional learning completed outside the duty day for paid non-duty days on September 21 and April 30. Students on the traditional calendar do not attend classes on those dates.

faqs.question: Does Austin ISD have school during Thanksgiving week in 2026?
faqs.answer: No. Austin ISD calls November 23-27 Fall Break, and students on the traditional calendar do not have regular classes during that Monday-Friday week.

faqs.question: Where can parents download the revised 2026-2027 calendar?
faqs.answer: Use the official PDF link on this page or visit Austin ISD’s calendar page.

editorialSummary.heading: How Austin ISD’s 2026-2027 ADSY calendar works
highlights: Eighteen optional summer instructional dates from July 7 through August 5
Seven optional Saturday sessions for eligible or invited students
Four early-release dates that differ from the traditional calendar
paragraphs: Austin ISD’s 2026-27 ADSY pilot applies only to participating campuses, not the district as a whole. The Board-approved announcement names nine campuses: Linder, Pecan Springs, Sanchez and Wooldridge elementary schools, plus Burnet, Dobie, Mendez, Paredes and Webb middle schools. The current ADSY calendar PDF header lists the same group except Paredes, so families at Paredes should confirm the campus calendar directly.

The current PDF marks 18 optional summer instructional dates from July 7 through Aug. 5 and seven optional Saturday sessions from October through April. Austin ISD says these extra summer and Saturday opportunities are for eligible or invited students and are not mandatory. The approved program design totals 25 optional additional days: 18 summer dates plus seven Saturdays.

Regular classes begin Aug. 18 and end May 27. The current ADSY PDF marks early release on Sept. 21, Nov. 3, Feb. 15 and Apr. 30. Austin ISD’s live ADSY page and March 26 Board announcement describe six half-days, so the district’s published sources are not fully consistent. Families should confirm unresolved schedule differences with their campus.

comparativeInsights: The 18 summer dates are split into five continuous weekday blocks; Fridays and weekends between blocks are not stored as ADSY attendance days.
The seven Saturday sessions are optional and intended for eligible or invited students, not every student enrolled at an ADSY campus.
September 21, November 3, February 15, and April 30 are early-release attendance days on the ADSY PDF rather than full student holidays.
October 9 and March 26 remain conditional because the PDF marks them as holidays and bad-weather make-up dates.

Austin ISD’s Board announcement names nine campuses, while the current ADSY PDF header lists eight and omits Paredes Middle School; Paredes families should confirm which calendar their campus is implementing.

faqs.question: What is Austin ISD ADSY?
faqs.answer: Additional Days School Year, or ADSY, is a state-funded, campus-specific program that adds optional summer and Saturday learning opportunities for students who need additional academic support.

faqs.question: Which Austin ISD schools use the 2026-2027 ADSY calendar?
faqs.answer: Austin ISD’s Board approval names nine campuses: Linder, Pecan Springs, Sanchez and Wooldridge elementary schools, and Burnet, Dobie, Mendez, Paredes and Webb middle schools. The current ADSY calendar PDF header omits Paredes, so Paredes families should confirm the calendar with their campus.

faqs.question: When do regular classes begin at ADSY campuses?
faqs.answer: Regular classes begin Tuesday, August 18, 2026, the same day as the rest of Austin ISD. Optional summer ADSY instruction starts earlier, on Tuesday, July 7.

faqs.question: What are the optional summer ADSY dates?
faqs.answer: The PDF marks July 7-9, July 13-16, July 20-23, July 27-30, and August 3-5. These are five separate blocks totaling 18 instructional dates, not one uninterrupted July-to-August session.

faqs.question: Are summer and Saturday ADSY sessions mandatory?
faqs.answer: No. Austin ISD says the extra summer and Saturday sessions are optional for eligible or invited students, although students recommended for accelerated instruction are strongly encouraged to participate.

faqs.question: Is Austin ISD ADSY the same as summer school?
faqs.answer: No. Austin ISD describes ADSY as a high-impact learning opportunity led by certified teachers, not traditional summer school. Its optional summer and Saturday sessions combine core instruction with enrichment activities.

faqs.question: Who is invited to Austin ISD’s optional ADSY sessions?
faqs.answer: Austin ISD says a subset of students who need additional academic support will be invited. Students recommended for extra support are strongly encouraged to attend, but the summer and Saturday sessions are optional.

faqs.question: What do students do on Austin ISD ADSY days?
faqs.answer: Austin ISD says ADSY days combine targeted grade-level instruction and small-group academic support with enrichment such as STEM, arts, music and sports. Summer participants receive core instruction as part of the program day.

faqs.question: When are the seven Saturday ADSY sessions?
faqs.answer: The calendar marks October 3, November 7, and December 5, 2026, followed by January 9, February 13, March 6, and April 3, 2027.

faqs.question: Which dates are early release on the current ADSY PDF?
faqs.answer: The current PDF marks September 21, November 3, February 15, and April 30 as early-release days. It does not publish dismissal times, so families should check their campus schedule.

faqs.question: Is October 9 an early-release day or a holiday?
faqs.answer: The current ADSY PDF marks October 9 as a student/staff holiday and possible bad-weather make-up day. The district’s current ADSY webpage lists October 9 among six proposed half-days, so families should confirm any update with their campus.

faqs.question: What is the ADSY schedule for November 2-3, 2026?
faqs.answer: The current ADSY PDF marks November 2 as a student/staff holiday and November 3 as an early-release day. Austin ISD’s live ADSY page still lists both dates among six proposed half-days, so families should confirm any updated campus schedule.

faqs.question: Are ADSY students off school on Austin ISD PLED days?
faqs.answer: Not in the same way as the traditional calendar. The current ADSY PDF marks September 21 and April 30 as early-release attendance days, while traditional-calendar students are off for PLED. Austin ISD’s ADSY staff FAQ also says staff at ADSY campuses do not participate in PLED.

faqs.question: Do ADSY students attend school on February 15?
faqs.answer: The current ADSY PDF says yes: February 15 is marked as an early-release attendance day. Austin ISD’s live ADSY program page still describes a different six-half-day schedule, so families should confirm any updated campus instructions.

faqs.question: Does Austin ISD provide transportation and meals for summer ADSY?
faqs.answer: Austin ISD says transportation and meals are provided during the optional summer program. Saturday sessions include snacks, but the district says transportation and meals are not available for those Saturdays.

faqs.question: When is fall break for ADSY campuses?
faqs.answer: Fall break runs Monday, November 23, through Friday, November 27, 2026. The ADSY calendar follows the same full Thanksgiving-week break as the traditional district calendar.

faqs.question: When do ADSY students return after winter break?
faqs.answer: Winter break is December 21 through January 1. January 4 is a student holiday for staff development, so regular classes resume Tuesday, January 5.

faqs.question: What are the ADSY spring break dates?
faqs.answer: Spring break runs Monday, March 15, through Friday, March 19, 2027. Students return Monday, March 22 unless Austin ISD announces a weather-related change.

faqs.question: Do ADSY students have school on October 12, 2026?
faqs.answer: The current ADSY PDF marks October 12 as a parent-conference/student-holiday date, so students do not attend regular classes. The calendar also notes Indigenous Peoples’ Day.

faqs.question: Do ADSY students have school on March 10, 2027?
faqs.answer: The current ADSY PDF marks March 10 as a parent-conference/student-holiday date. Austin ISD’s live ADSY program page still lists March 10 in a different proposed six-half-day schedule, so families should confirm any campus update.

faqs.question: How many additional instructional days does ADSY offer?
faqs.answer: The approved design provides 25 optional extra opportunities: 18 summer dates and seven Saturday sessions. Regular early-release days are part of the 175-day school calendar, not additional dates.

faqs.question: How many regular school days do Austin ISD ADSY campuses have?
faqs.answer: Austin ISD’s Board announcement describes 175 regular school days for participating ADSY campuses. The 18 optional summer dates and seven optional Saturdays are additional opportunities outside that regular calendar.

faqs.question: Does Austin ISD ADSY cost families anything?
faqs.answer: No. Austin ISD says ADSY is provided at no cost to families.

faqs.question: Why is Paredes Middle School missing from the PDF?
faqs.answer: The current ADSY PDF header lists eight campuses and does not name Paredes. Austin ISD’s Board announcement and current ADSY webpage both include Paredes, so Paredes families should ask the campus which calendar applies.

faqs.question: Why do Austin ISD’s ADSY webpage and calendar PDF show different information?
faqs.answer: Austin ISD’s current sources are not fully consistent. The PDF shows 18 summer dates, four early-release dates and eight campuses; the webpage describes 19 summer days, six half-days and nine campuses. The Board announcement lists 18 summer days, six half-days and nine campuses.

faqs.question: How is the ADSY calendar different from Austin ISD’s traditional calendar?
faqs.answer: ADSY adds optional summer and Saturday instruction and changes several traditional student holidays into shortened attendance days. The regular first day, last day, fall break, winter break, and spring break remain aligned.

faqs.question: Could March 26 become a required school day?
faqs.answer: On the current ADSY PDF, yes. March 26 is marked as a student/staff holiday and bad-weather make-up day, so it could become an attendance day if Austin ISD activates it. The live ADSY page still lists March 26 in a different proposed half-day schedule, so families should confirm any update with their campus.

faqs.question: Where can families download the official ADSY calendar?
faqs.answer: Use the official ADSY PDF link on this page or visit Austin ISD’s calendar page. The district’s ADSY program page provides separate details about eligibility, meals, transportation, and optional participation.

statistics.label: Student attendance days
statistics.explanation: Austin ISD’s March 2026 board announcement describes 175 regular school days for the ADSY pilot.

statistics.label: Total no-school weekdays
statistics.explanation: Counted from districtwide no-class events between the first and last student days. Weekends and shortened school days are excluded, and overlapping events count once.

statistics.label: Student no-school days
statistics.explanation: Counts weekdays without regular classes outside holidays and multi-day breaks, including staff or planning days. Overlapping entries count once.

statistics.label: Listed early-release dates
statistics.explanation: Counted from official early-release entries; some dates apply only to the grades or campuses named in the calendar.

statistics.label: Longest listed break
statistics.explanation: Dec 19, 2026–Jan 4, 2027, including weekends. The stretch contains 11 confirmed no-school weekdays.

statistics.label: Long weekends
statistics.explanation: Counts three- or four-day no-school stretches formed by a weekend plus one or two confirmed weekday closures. Longer school breaks are excluded.

statistics.label: Full-week breaks
statistics.explanation: Counts continuous no-school stretches containing at least five confirmed weekdays without regular classes. Adjacent holidays and weekends remain part of the same break.
